subject.title: [Bug] Telegram exec approval bubble not dismissed after clicking approve

question: Should maintainers adopt, close, or replace the currently linked fork PR for the Telegram approval-message deletion fix?
rationale: The source-level bug is clear and the same-repo PRs are closed, but GitHub still links an open fork PR with closing syntax, so repair automation should not create a duplicate target until maintainers choose the landing path.

options.title: Adopt or replace the candidate
options.body: Review the linked fork PR and either land its narrow active-runtime fix in openclaw/openclaw or close it and authorize a replacement.

options.title: Queue a fresh fix
options.body: If the fork PR is not viable, clear the linked-candidate state and queue a focused fix against the active Telegram runtime.

options.title: Wait on the fork PR
options.body: Leave the issue open without new automation while waiting for the fork PR author to make it reviewable.

recommendation.title: Adopt or replace the candidate
recommendation.body: Review the linked fork PR and either land its narrow active-runtime fix in openclaw/openclaw or close it and authorize a replacement.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the native approval lifecycle and are the strongest history signal for the final-action seam involved here.
